article.title: Next Generation Seismic Source Detection by Computer Vision: Untangling the Complexity of the 2016 Kaikōura Earthquake Sequence
article.journal: Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth
article.scientific_question: Can computer-vision source scanning and guided phase picking detect and locate the dense 2016 Kaikōura sequence, and can a quality-controlled subset be precisely relocated?
article.sequence: 2016 Mw 7.8 Kaikōura earthquake and immediate aftershock sequence
article.catalog_relationship: Introduces SUGAR and publishes an event catalog (S10), a GrowClust-relocated intermediate product (S11), and focal-mechanism products (S12).

evidence.note: Supplementary material contains construction details and data products.

construction_workflow.summary: GeoNet waveforms from a 46-station network are preprocessed into source-scanning brightness videos, analyzed by a 3-D U-Net, merged into candidates, phase-picked and associated, located and magnitude-estimated, then relatively relocated with GrowClust and cluster-filtered.

input_data.name: GeoNet seismic waveforms
input_data.temporal_spatial_scope: 2016-11-13 to 2016-12-31; northern South Island Kaikōura region
input_data.channels_sampling: Vertical and two horizontal channels; sample rate not specified in current extraction.
input_data.availability_conditions: 9 selected stations had approximately ±1 s timing errors; paper reports little effect.

stages.name: waveform preprocessing and source scanning
stages.purpose: Create source-scanning brightness videos from the regional waveform network.
stages.method: 5–20 Hz filtering; stack 1.5 s before to 4.5 s after predicted arrivals; 4 km horizontal grid and fixed 10 km initial depth.
stages.intermediate_result: Brightness videos and local maxima candidates.
stages.dependencies: Sequence-specific station geometry and predicted arrivals.

stages.name: 3-D U-Net source segmentation
stages.purpose: Predict source locations and identify candidate maxima in the 3-D source volume.
qc_and_rejection_rules: Synthetic test precision reported >0.93 at selected threshold; this is not the real-event catalog precision.
stages.analyst_intervention: Model trained on synthetic samples; no event-catalog labels used for training.

evidence.locator: Sections 2.1–3.1, 3-D U-Net architecture/training paragraphs and real-data threshold

stages.name: candidate merging and guided phase picking
stages.purpose: Convert source candidates into phase observations suitable for association.
stages.method: Candidate merging followed by Earthquake Transformer guided picking on the real data.
qc_and_rejection_rules: Delete candidate if fewer than two qualified P or two qualified S phases.
stages.analyst_intervention: No routine manual picking reported; mainshock and largest aftershock are manually inserted later from GeoNet solutions.

evidence.locator: Section 2.2.3, candidate merging and guided P/S picking paragraph
evidence.note: Guided P/S picking and minimum phase rules.

stages.name: phase association and maximum-intersection location
stages.purpose: Associate phases to events and refine hypocenters.
stages.method: Distance-dependent P/S residual association and maximum-intersection search.
qc_and_rejection_rules: Fewer than two qualified P or two qualified S phases deletes candidate.
Retain when Q_e >= 0.6 or total phase count >= 10.
stages.analyst_intervention: GeoNet mainshock and largest aftershock solutions manually added.
stages.dependencies: Distance-dependent residual thresholds and velocity model.

stages.name: local magnitude estimation
stages.purpose: Estimate local magnitudes for associated located events.
stages.method: Local Richter-style equation with synthesized Wood–Anderson amplitudes, Rhoades et al. (2021) constants, P-wave amplitude factor-of-two correction, and station correction in final pass.
stages.software_or_model: Rhoades et al. (2021) magnitude constants; synthetic Wood–Anderson response

evidence.locator: Sections 2.2.3–2.2.4, local-magnitude equation and station-correction paragraph

stages.name: waveform differential-time relocation
stages.purpose: Improve relative locations for a quality-controlled event subset.
stages.method: 1–10 Hz waveform cross-correlation on 2 s P/S windows followed by GrowClust.

parameters.name: pair_support
parameters.note: At least eight coefficients above threshold.

qc_and_rejection_rules: Event pairs require at least eight coefficients above 0.65.
stages.dependencies: S10 event hypotheses and waveform availability.

evidence.locator: Section 4, GrowClust relocation paragraph and Supplementary Table S11 description

evidence.note: S11 fields and local row count.

stages.name: cluster filtering and supplementary mechanisms
stages.purpose: Select dense clusters for the final high-quality set and provide focal mechanisms.
stages.method: Retain clusters with at least 10 events; focal mechanisms provided separately.
qc_and_rejection_rules: S11 is an intermediate release; final cluster membership is not separately archived locally.
stages.intermediate_result: Article reports 41,392 events; local S12 has 55 rows.
stages.analyst_intervention: Large-event manual insertion occurs before this stage.

evidence.locator: Section 4, cluster-size filtering paragraph and Supplementary Table S12 discussion

scientific_findings.statement: The dense SUGAR catalog resolves complex overlapping seismicity, while the final cluster-filtered set is intended as a high-quality relative-geometry product.
Absolute locations are expected to have errors of a few kilometres, whereas relative bootstrap uncertainties are reported below 1 km.

benchmark_context.quality_interpretation: Q2 dense-detection/association and relative-relocation reference; metric-specific Q1 for the reported clustered relative geometry only.
benchmark_context.recommended_role: Primary target for dense event recovery, phase association, and relative relocation stress tests in the Kaikōura case.
benchmark_context.comparison_or_baseline_sources: Compare with Lanza/Chamberlain products and GeoNet operational baseline only after identical time/space/depth masks.
benchmark_context.valid_comparisons: Event recovery, origin-time, relative geometry, cluster structure, phase support, and station-coverage metrics.
benchmark_context.caveats: Shared GeoNet observations reduce observational independence; SUGAR model is site-specific; do not treat S11 as the final 41,392-row file.
